title: Reported Speech
subject: english_grammar
syllabus_note: Follows the CBSE 2025-26 English Language and Literature (184) syllabus, Section B Grammar: reported speech (commands and requests, statements, questions), tested through gap filling, editing and transformation.

blocks.title: How do you pass on a message?
blocks.body:
Your friend says to you on the phone: *"I am not well. I can't come to school today."* Your teacher asks why she is absent. You don't repeat her exact words; you say:

*She said that she **was** not well and **couldn't** come to school **that day**.*

Notice what changed: *I → she*, *am → was*, *can't → couldn't*, *today → that day*. That is **reported (indirect) speech**. Every CBSE board paper asks you to report a dialogue or complete a reported sentence, usually two or three marks' worth. Once you know the four changes, it becomes the easiest scoring question in the paper.

blocks.title: The reporter of rural India
blocks.body:
For decades, journalist P. Sainath travelled through India's villages, listening to farmers, labourers and women, and reported their words to the whole country. His book *Everybody Loves a Good Drought* became a classic of Indian journalism.

He received the Ramon Magsaysay Award in 2007. A good reporter passes on people's words accurately, without changing their meaning; that is exactly what reported speech trains you to do.
blocks.future: Reporting skills are at the heart of journalism, law, police work, research interviews and business communication.

blocks.question: Riya said, "I am tired." Which is the correct reported form?
options: Riya said that she was tired.
Riya said that I am tired.
Riya said that she is tired yesterday.
blocks.explanation: *I* becomes *she* (Riya), and *am* moves back to *was* because the reporting verb *said* is in the past.

blocks.title: Pronouns, tense, time and place, and the joining word
blocks.body:
In *She said, "I am busy today."*, *She said* is the **reporting verb** and *"I am busy today"* is the **reported speech**.

When we change direct speech into indirect speech, check four things:

1. **Reporting verb and joining word:** *said → said/told*; add *that*, *if/whether*, a wh- word, or *to*.
2. **Pronouns** change to fit the new speaker: *"I love **my** dog," said Ravi.* → *Ravi said that **he** loved **his** dog.* Use the **SON** rule: **S**ubject-pronoun (I, we) changes to match the **s**ubject of the reporting verb; **O**bject-pronoun (you) changes to match the **o**bject; **N**o change for third-person pronouns (he, she, they).
3. **Tense moves one step back** when the reporting verb is in the past (*said, told, asked*).
4. **Time and place words** change: *now → then, today → that day, here → there*.

**When the tense does NOT change:**
- The reporting verb is in the present or future: *He **says**, "I **am** busy."* → *He **says** that he **is** busy.*
- The reported speech is a universal truth, a habitual fact or a proverb: *The teacher said, "The sun **rises** in the east."* → *... that the sun **rises** in the east.*
- The direct speech already has *would, could, should, might, ought to, had (past perfect)*.

blocks.title: Tense change (backshift)
blocks.body:
| Direct speech | Reported speech | Example (*He said, "..."* → *He said that ...*) |
|---|---|---|
| simple present | simple past | *"I **like** tea."* → he **liked** tea |
| present continuous | past continuous | *"I **am reading**."* → he **was reading** |
| present perfect | past perfect | *"I **have finished**."* → he **had finished** |
| present perfect continuous | past perfect continuous | *"I **have been waiting**."* → he **had been waiting** |
| simple past | past perfect | *"I **saw** her."* → he **had seen** her |
| past continuous | past perfect continuous | *"I **was sleeping**."* → he **had been sleeping** |
| will / shall | would / should | *"I **will** come."* → he **would** come |
| can / may | could / might | *"I **can** swim."* → he **could** swim |
| must | must / had to | *"I **must** go."* → he **had to** go |
| past perfect, would, could, should, might, ought to | no change | *"You **should** rest."* → I **should** rest |

blocks.title: Time and place words
blocks.body:
| Direct | Reported |
|---|---|
| now | then |
| today | that day |
| tonight | that night |
| yesterday | the day before / the previous day |
| tomorrow | the next day / the following day |
| last week | the week before / the previous week |
| next week | the following week |
| ago | before |
| this / these | that / those |
| here | there |
| come | go (often) |

blocks.question: He said, "I will meet you tomorrow." → He said that he ____ me ____.
option_feedback: After *said*, *will → would* and *tomorrow → the next day*.

blocks.title: said or told?
blocks.body:
- **said** has no object, or *said to* + object: *He **said** (to me) that he was hungry.*
- **told** must have an object: *He **told me** that he was hungry.* (✗ *He told that ...*, ✗ *He said me ...*)
- In indirect speech, *said to me* usually becomes **told me**.

Other useful reporting verbs for statements: *replied, answered, informed, added, explained, admitted, complained, promised, assured, remarked*. Board examiners reward a precise verb: *"Yes, I broke the vase," said Raju.* → *Raju **admitted** that he **had broken** the vase.*

**Worked steps:** *Meena said to me, "I have lost my book here."*
1. *said to me* → **told me**; add **that**.
2. *I → she* (Meena); *my → her*.
3. *have lost → had lost*.
4. *here → there*.

→ *Meena told me that she had lost her book there.*

blocks.question: Mother said to me, "You must finish your homework now." → Mother told me that I ____ my homework ____.
option_feedback: That changes the meaning: she gave an instruction, not news of a finished action.
*now* must change to *then*, and *must* (obligation) usually becomes *had to*.
After *told*, the tense goes back: *had to*.

blocks.title: Questions become statements
blocks.body:
When we report a question, it **stops being a question**:
- Use *asked, enquired, wanted to know, wondered*.
- **Word order becomes subject + verb** (like a statement).
- **No question mark** at the end, and **no *do/does/did***.

**Yes/no questions** (starting with a helping verb: *Is, Are, Do, Did, Can, Will, Have ...*) → use **if** or **whether**:
*He said to me, "**Are you** coming?"* → *He asked me **if I was** coming.*
*She said, "**Do you** like music?"* → *She asked **whether I liked** music.*

**Wh- questions** (*what, where, when, why, who, how, which*) → keep the wh- word, then subject + verb:
*The teacher said, "**Where do you live**?"* → *The teacher asked me **where I lived**.*
*He said, "**Why did you come** late?"* → *He asked me **why I had come** late.*

✗ *He asked me where did I live.* ✓ *He asked me where I lived.*
✗ *She asked me that if I was ready.* ✓ *She asked me if I was ready.*

blocks.question: Rohan said to Priya, "Where are you going?" → Rohan asked Priya ____.
blocks.explanation: wh- word + subject + verb, tense moved back.
option_feedback: Reported questions use statement order: subject + verb.

blocks.question: The shopkeeper said to me, "Do you want a bag?" → The shopkeeper asked me ____.
blocks.explanation: Yes/no question → *if/whether* + subject + verb, tense moved back.
option_feedback: Reported questions lose *do* and the question order.

blocks.title: Choosing the reporting verb
blocks.body:
| Type of sentence | Reporting verb | Joining word | Pattern |
|---|---|---|---|
| Statement | said, told + object, replied, informed, added, explained | that | *She told me **that** she was busy.* |
| Yes/no question | asked, enquired, wanted to know, wondered | if / whether | *He asked **if** I was ready.* |
| Wh- question | asked, enquired, wanted to know | the wh- word | *She asked **where** I lived.* |
| Command | ordered, commanded, told, directed, instructed | to / not to + V1 | *The teacher told us **to** sit down.* |
| Request | requested, begged, asked | to / not to + V1 | *He requested me **to** help him.* |
| Advice | advised, warned, suggested | to + V1 / that … should | *The doctor advised him **to** rest.* |
| Exclamation / wish | exclaimed with joy/sorrow, wished, prayed | that | *She exclaimed with joy that it was a beautiful view.* |

blocks.title: to + V1 and not to + V1
blocks.body:
Imperative sentences (orders, requests, advice) are reported with a verb that shows the **tone**, then **to + V1**:

- Command: *The officer said to the soldiers, "Stand still."* → *The officer **ordered** the soldiers **to stand** still.*
- Request (*please*): *She said to me, "Please lend me your pen."* → *She **requested** me **to lend** her my pen.* (*please* disappears; *requested* carries the politeness)
- Negative command: *Mother said, "Don't touch the stove."* → *Mother **told** me **not to touch** the stove.* (*Don't* → *not to*)
- Advice: *The doctor said, "You should rest."* → *The doctor **advised** him **to rest**.*
- Warning: *"Don't swim here," said the guard.* → *The guard **warned** us **not to swim** there.*
- Suggestion with *Let's*: *He said, "Let's play chess."* → *He **suggested that we should play** chess.* (or *suggested playing chess*). ✗ *suggested us to play*

**Polite questions that are really requests** (*Could you…? Will you…? Would you…?*) are usually reported with *requested/asked + to*: *"Could you open the window?"* → *She **requested** me **to open** the window.*

blocks.question: The teacher said to the students, "Don't make a noise." → The teacher ____ the students ____ a noise.
blocks.explanation: Negative command → *told/ordered + object + not to + V1*.
option_feedback: *Don't* changes to *not to* in reported speech.
*said* cannot take a direct object like *the students*.

blocks.question: He said, "Let us go for a picnic." → He ____ go for a picnic.
blocks.explanation: *Let us/Let's* → *suggested that we should* + V1 (or *suggested going*).
option_feedback: The words of the speaker must be reported, not repeated.
*Let us* is a suggestion, not an order.

blocks.title: How the board asks it
blocks.body:
The board usually gives a short dialogue and asks you to **complete** the reported version, or to choose the correct reported sentence. Example:

*Customer: Can you show me a cheaper phone?*
*Shopkeeper: I'm afraid this is the cheapest one we have.*

Report: *The customer asked the shopkeeper **if he could show him a cheaper phone**. The shopkeeper replied **that he was afraid that was the cheapest one they had**.*

**Checklist before you write:**
1. What type of sentence is it? (statement / question / command / request)
2. Which reporting verb and joining word?
3. Pronouns: who is speaking to whom?
4. Tense one step back.
5. Time and place words.
6. Question → statement order, no *?*, no *do/did*.

blocks.title: Reporting a dialogue step by step
blocks.problem:
Report the dialogue:

*Teacher: Why didn't you submit your project yesterday, Aman?*
*Aman: I was ill, Ma'am. I will submit it tomorrow.*
*Teacher: Make sure you bring a medical certificate.*
steps: Line 1 is a wh- question → *asked Aman why*; *didn't you submit* → *he had not submitted* (no *did*, past → past perfect); *yesterday → the day before*.
→ *The teacher asked Aman why he had not submitted his project the day before.*
Line 2 is a statement → *replied (respectfully) that*; *I was ill → he had been ill*; *I will submit → he would submit*; *tomorrow → the next day*.
→ *Aman replied respectfully that he had been ill and that he would submit it the next day.*
Line 3 is a command/advice → *told/instructed him to make sure he brought*.
→ *The teacher told him to make sure that he brought a medical certificate.*
blocks.answer: The teacher asked Aman why he had not submitted his project the day before. Aman replied respectfully that he had been ill and would submit it the next day. The teacher told him to make sure that he brought a medical certificate.

blocks.title: Editing a reported sentence
blocks.problem:
Correct the errors:

1. She asked me where did I live.
2. He told that he was tired.
3. The doctor advised me that take rest.
4. I asked him whether is he ready.
steps: 2. *told* needs an object: **told me that** (or *said that*).
3. Advice → *to* + V1: **advised me to take rest**.
blocks.answer: where I lived; told me / said that; advised me to take rest; whether he was ready

blocks.question: Neha: "Have you seen my keys?" → Neha asked me ____.
options: whether I have seen my keys
that I had seen her keys
whether I had seen her keys
whether had I seen her keys
blocks.explanation: Yes/no question → *whether* + statement order; present perfect → past perfect; *my → her*.
option_feedback: *have seen → had seen*, and *my → her* (Neha's keys).

blocks.title: The "P-T-T-W" check
blocks.body:
Before writing any reported sentence, tick **P-T-T-W**:
- **P**ronouns: who is speaking to whom?
- **T**ense: one step back (*is → was, was → had been, will → would*).
- **T**ime/place: *now → then, today → that day, here → there*.
- **W**ord to join: *that* (statement), *if/whether* (yes/no), wh- (wh- question), *to / not to* (command).

**Question → statement**: drop the *?*, drop *do/did*, put the subject before the verb.
**Don't → not to.** **Please → requested.** **Let's → suggested that we should.**

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.body:
1. ✗ *He told that ...* ✓ *He told me that ... / He said that ...*
2. ✗ *She asked me where was I going.* ✓ *She asked me where I was going.*
3. ✗ *He asked me that if I was ready.* ✓ *He asked me if I was ready.*
4. ✗ *Mother told me don't go out.* ✓ *Mother told me not to go out.*
5. ✗ *She requested me please to help.* ✓ *She requested me to help her.*
6. ✗ *He said that he will come tomorrow.* ✓ *He said that he would come the next day.*
7. ✗ *The teacher said that the earth moved round the sun.* ✓ *... moves round the sun.*
8. ✗ *He suggested us to go.* ✓ *He suggested that we should go.*
9. ✗ *She asked did I like it.* ✓ *She asked if I liked it.*
10. Forgetting the pronoun: ✗ *Ravi said that I was hungry* (when Ravi meant himself) ✓ *Ravi said that he was hungry.*

blocks.title: Try this in class
blocks.body: Play **"Chinese whispers with grammar"**: student A whispers a sentence to B (*"I'll bring my guitar tomorrow"*); B reports it aloud to the class (*"Aditi said that she would bring her guitar the next day"*). The class checks P-T-T-W. Then use real dialogues from the First Flight chapters (e.g. *The Proposal*) and report them line by line.

blocks.title: Say it in your own words
blocks.body: Why does *"Where do you live?"* become *where I lived* and not *where did I live*? Explain the rule to a friend.

blocks.title: Where this leads
blocks.body:
- **Chapter 1, Tenses:** the sequence of tenses drives every backshift.
- **Chapter 2, Modals:** *can → could, may → might, will → would, must → had to*.
- **Literature:** questions on *The Proposal*, *Madam Rides the Bus* and *Two Gentlemen of Verona* often ask what a character said: answer in reported speech.

blocks.title: Mastery challenge
blocks.body:
Report the dialogue:

*Passenger: Excuse me, does this bus go to the railway station?*
*Conductor: Yes, it does. Please sit down; we are leaving now.*

**Answer:** *The passenger politely asked the conductor whether that bus went to the railway station. The conductor replied that it did, and requested him to sit down as they were leaving then.*

blocks.title: Chapter summary
blocks.body:
- Reported speech passes on someone's words without quoting them.
- Change pronouns, move the tense back (after a past reporting verb), change time/place words, and add the right joining word.
- Statements → *said/told + that*; yes/no questions → *asked + if/whether*; wh- questions → *asked + wh-*; commands/requests → *told/ordered/requested + (not) to + V1*.
- Reported questions use statement order, no *do/did*, no question mark.
- No backshift when the reporting verb is present/future, or for universal truths.

blocks.title: Board exam tips
blocks.body:
- Use a precise reporting verb (*requested, ordered, advised, enquired, replied, exclaimed*); it shows understanding.
- Never put a question mark at the end of a reported question.
- When completing a reported sentence, copy the given beginning exactly and continue from it.
- Check that your final sentence is grammatical on its own: read it aloud in your head.

blocks.back: He asked me **if/whether I was** ready.

blocks.front: "Don't run," the teacher said to us. →
blocks.back: The teacher **told us not to run**.
